[spoiler=Confusion sets in as State Election results are released belatedly]  
[i]Wellassonan National News - Новеллсти Нациоьнлыы Веласоньый. Saturday, 14 August 2027[/i]
After a long anticipated wait, the Electoral Commission has finally announced the results of the elections held on 29 July. Despite the fact that only 2 states held their elections this year, it took nearly 16 days for the results to be published, which is highly unusual, given that past elections had been announced in only 4-5 days.

Nevertheless, In Utveyush, Socialist Ulyanha Shenchet easily won a second term as premier, winning 46% of the vote, far outcompeting her competitors. The legislative race played out in a similar manner, Managing to will all 3 senate seats that they previously held, as well as winning an extra seat in the Diet, bringing their total in the state up to 5. This victory, while expected, was massive for the Socialists, who have been dealing with a myriad of problems resulting from the unpopularity of PM Sokolova's policies.

In Kemder, it was predicted that Ivan Rometenko of the Unity party would turn out victorious by all major news sources prior to the election. However, in the end, far-right Reform the State candidate Karina Lagounov ended up winning the election by an slim margin. Lagounov won about 35% of the vote, with Rometenko winning just under 33%, and Socialist candidate Kaldangan Kemurtevich winning only 19% of the vote in a severe underperformance. Reform the State also won a plurality of Senate and Diet seats as well.  Political pundits theorize the general unpopularity of Socialist policies in Kemder led much of the populace to vote for the far-right candidate instead, despite the centrist Unity party being historically supported in the state. This election marks the first time in Wellassonan history in which a far-right candidate will hold the Premiership in a state, as well as holding the most Senate and Diet seats of a state as well.

A lot of controversy has surrounded this election, particularly around the belated announcement of the results. Lagounov has criticised the delay of the results, calling them an attempt to falsify the vote count and keep her from winning the election. In an interview shortly after the results were announced, she said, [i]"There were clear attempts at undermining democracy this election. The radical left has already infiltrated the electoral process, and it is only a matter of time until they turn us back into the communist days. The free and fair election process must be protected by law and rid of partisanship."[/i] Socialist candidate Kemurtevich hit back at Lagounov shortly after, stating, [i]"[Lagounov] is the only one undermining democracy right now."[/i]

Lagounov is expected to take office in early October. The next elections for both states, as well as Fergecko due to the changes in election schedule, are set for 29 July 2031.
[/spoiler]

[pre]PRESIDENT OF THE NATION                

       Part 1/3[/pre]

[spoiler=
[pre]Ladies and Gentlemen, we present to you:    
    President of the Nation, Yusuf Al-Mansoori![/pre]]

Yusuf Al-Mansoori sat at the presidential desk. A camera was pointed at him, and a recording crew buzzed around the room. The presidents brother, Faris Al-Mansoori, stood next to Yusuf.

[i]Well be live soon, are you ready?[/i]

Yusuf laughed. [i]Ive been ready. You know I have been preparing for this moment since I began my campaigning.[/i]

Faris smiled, remembering all the times Yusuf joked that he was live in front of the nation as president, not only during the political campaign, but also throughout his childhood. Now, standing beside him as the crew prepared to broadcast his speech to the nation, Faris couldnt help but feel a sense of accomplishment for what they have done together.

[i]Were live in one minute![/i] a cameraman shouted out.

[i]Thank you,[/i] Yusuf replied, nodding in acknowledgement to the man. He straightened his tie and adjusted his posture. 

[i]You sure you dont want a script?[/i] Faris asked.

The president shook his head. [i]I never used one before, and I dont need to start now. I know just what Im going to say to them.[/i]

Faris nodded. [i]You better.[/i] He lightly punched his brothers shoulder.

[i]I tell you, Faris, that after this speech is done, I will recite it to you word for word. I know I can do it.[/i]

[i]How much do you want to bet?[/i]

[i]Live in thirty seconds![/i] the same camera man called out.

Yusuf laughed. [i]Youre ambitious, Ill say that. It hasnt even been a full day since Ive taken office and youre already trying to beat the president at something.[/i]

[i]Im just saying, I dont know how you can do it. No tricks, just you and your power of recitation.[/i]

[i]Its a gift of mine, brother,[/i] Yusuf said, [i]you know you have your own as well.[/i]

[i]Ten seconds![/i]

Faris stepped away from his brother, letting him prepare for his speech.

The red light on the camera turned on, showing that it was live. Yusuf bowed his head for a short prayer before looking up at the camera. He took a deep breath in and smiled.

[i][pre]Greetings, citizens of Hydronia! I am Yusuf Al-Mansoori, your newly elected president by the Parliament of our great nation![/pre][/i]

He smiled again, waiting a little bit before continuing.

[i][pre]I have many plans for this nation. We are in a position of great power, but at the same time, we are at a crossroads. We must know which is the right way in order to maintain our autonomy, and in order to maintain our special position on the world stage. Through a series of reforms and proposed laws, I intend to change the industry of Hydronia in order to increase our output, and thus our power on the world stage, and most importantly, the quality of life for every citizen throughout our territory![/pre][/i]

[i][pre]Now, this does mean we will have to change some of our policies, especially of how we conduct ourselves on the world stage. Some may believe that this is not worth it. But I believe it will be. After all, I am the president of Hydronia, and I seek what is best for this country. Much of the international stage is of secondary interest to me. This does not mean I will neglect the foreign relations of Hydronia, no, not at all, but rather that I will curate these relations to have what is best for us.[/pre][/i]

He paused for a small while.

[i][pre]There is much work to do, but we will persevere, together. After all, there is nothing that can be done against us when we are united in the same fight. We will come to improve our great nation to even greater heights. But, before I leave you all, I have one quick announcement to make. I would like to introduce my dearly cherished younger brother to you all; it is because of him that I am here now as your president![/pre][/i]

Yusuf stood, beckoning for his brother to join him. The camera panned upward to get a better view. After a bit of hesitation, Faris obliged, stepping into view of the camera. The president wrapped his arm around his brother and faced the camera.

[i][pre]This is my brother! He has supported me throughout my campaign, and is fit for a position in the high command of our politics, which is why I am making him my right hand man.[/pre][/i]

Faris smiled uneasily, while Yusuf beamed. The younger brother waved at the camera.

[i]Yusuf, thats enough[/i] Faris whispered, barely audible. Yusuf nodded and let his brother stand a bit off center from the camera.

[i][pre]That concludes todays speech. I kept it relatively short, since you will most definitely see more of what I have to say in speeches to other government bodies. I thank you for your attention. Have a good day, all.[/pre][/i]

Yusuf smiled at the camera, and Faris did, too. The blinking red light of the camera went dark.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=
Al-Mansoori Brothers]

Shortly after the broadcast, the two brothers walked together through the halls of the presidential palace.

[i]You know,[/i] Faris started, [i]that wasnt half bad.[/i]

Yusuf smiled. He knew his brother well enough to know that was the most sincere compliment he could give. [i]Thank you, brother.[/i]

[i]Whats next for today?[/i]

[i]Theres not much. Just come to the lounge and well relax a bit. Surely we deserve it after all that we did to get here.[/i]

Faris nodded. [i]Thats right, Im feeling tired after all that.[/i]

[i]It was just some presence in front of a camera, it wasnt that bad.[/i]

He sighed. [i]You know how much I dislike that. I dont like to have to make public appearances when its not needed, and when they are needed, I need time.[/i]

Yusuf frowned. [i]Come on, Im sure youll grow more used to these kinds of things. Public speaking, being in front of a crowd, these are things that get easier the more you do them. If you dont want to be in front of a camera, how are you going to give a speech to Parliament?[/i]

[i]I can do [b]that[/b], I just dont like it. But this is a job, and like any other, liking it isnt part of the requirements.[/i]

The older brother sighed. 

The pair arrived at the lounge soon after. While Yusuf opened the door and entered, holding it for his younger brother, Faris stopped by the doorway, thinking for a little while. After his pause, he spoke up. [i]I think Im going to take a short nap or something. Its been a long day for me and Im not feeling like staying up any longer.[/i]

[i]Alright, well, Ill see you later.[/i] Yusuf smiled.

Faris closed the door and walked to his chambers.

[/spoiler]
